text: What comes next: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, ___?
why: These are the days of the week in order, and Wednesday is followed by Thursday.

text: How many months of the year have 28 days?
why: Every month has at least 28 days; February is simply the only one that stops there.

text: Which of these is the odd one out: Apple, Banana, Carrot, Cherry?
why: Apple, banana and cherry are fruits; a carrot is a vegetable.

text: If you rearrange the letters of LISTEN you get a word that means 'quiet'. What is it?
why: LISTEN and SILENT use exactly the same six letters: L, I, S, T, E, N.

text: A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 run away. How many sheep are left?
why: "All but 9 run away" means every sheep except 9 left, so 9 remain.

text: Which word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?
why: Add the two letters E and R to SHORT and you get SHORTER.

text: What is the next number: 2, 4, 8, 16, ___?
why: Each number doubles the one before: 16 × 2 = 32.

text: If there are three apples and you take away two, how many do YOU have?
why: You took two apples, so you have two; the one left behind isn't yours.

text: Which of these words is spelt the same backwards: LEVEL, TABLE, CHAIR, HOUSE?
why: LEVEL is a palindrome: L-E-V-E-L reads the same in both directions.

text: Mary's father has five daughters: Nana, Nene, Nini, Nono and ___?
why: The question starts "Mary's father", so Mary herself is the fifth daughter.

text: What has a face and two hands but no arms or legs?
why: A clock has a face and an hour hand and a minute hand, but no arms or legs.

text: Which number is missing: 5, 10, 15, ___, 25?
why: The numbers go up in fives: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25.

text: What is the only number that has the same number of letters as its value?
why: FOUR has four letters; ONE, TWO and SIX have three, FIVE and NINE have four, and none of the others match.

text: How many times can you subtract 5 from 25?
why: You can subtract 5 from 25 only once; after that you're subtracting from 20.

text: Which letter comes next: J, F, M, A, M, J, ___?
why: These are the initials of the months: January, February, March, April, May, June, then July.

text: If EARTH has a HEART, which body part does MARS have? (rearrange the letters)
why: EARTH is an anagram of HEART, and MARS rearranges to ARMS.

text: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
why: MINUTE has one M, MOMENT has two and A THOUSAND YEARS has none.

text: I am an odd number. Take away one letter and I become even. What number am I?
why: Take the S off SEVEN and you're left with EVEN.

text: A clock shows 3:15. What is the angle between the hour and minute hands, in degrees?
why: At 3:15 the minute hand is on the 3, but the hour hand has moved a quarter of 30°, which is 7.5°, past it.

text: What is the next letter in this sequence: O, T, T, F, F, S, S, E, ___?
why: These are the initials of One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, Seven, Eight, so next is N for Nine.

text: Which of these is NOT a girl's name when said aloud: LC, KT, IV, EW?
why: Said aloud, LC is Elsie, KT is Katie and IV is Ivy, but EW is no name.

text: How many sides does a hexagon have multiplied by the number of sides on a triangle?
why: A hexagon has 6 sides and a triangle has 3, and 6 × 3 = 18.

text: If you write down all the numbers from 1 to 100, how many times do you write the digit 9?
why: The units digit is 9 ten times (9, 19 ... 99) and the tens digit is 9 ten times (90 to 99), which makes 20.

text: Which word can go before all of these to make new words: BOARD, HOLE, NOTE?
why: KEYBOARD, KEYHOLE and KEYNOTE.

text: Which is heavier: a kilogram of feathers or a kilogram of bricks?
why: A kilogram is a kilogram, so both weigh exactly 1 kg.

text: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. Each catches one fish, yet only three fish are caught in total. How is that possible?
why: There are only three of them: the grandfather and the father are both fathers, and the father and the son are both sons.

text: What is the next number: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ___?
why: This is the Fibonacci sequence, where each number is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21.

text: How many squares are there on a chessboard? Not just the small ones.
why: Count the squares of each size from 1×1 to 8×8: 64 + 49 + 36 + 25 + 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 204.

text: If it takes 5 machines 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, how long does it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets?
why: Each machine takes 5 minutes to make one widget, so 100 machines make 100 widgets in the same 5 minutes.

text: A bat and a ball cost £1.10 together. The bat costs £1 more than the ball. How much is the ball, in pence?
why: If the ball costs 5p, the bat costs £1.05, and 5p + £1.05 = £1.10.

text: What is the missing number: 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ___?
why: The gaps go up by 2 each time (3, 5, 7, 9), so the next gap is 11: 27 + 11 = 38.

text: How many letters are in THE ALPHABET?
why: THE has 3 letters and ALPHABET has 8, so THE ALPHABET has 11.

text: What do these have in common: BOOKKEEPER, COMMITTEE, BALLOON?
why: Each word has two double letters side by side: bOOKKEEper, commiTTEE, baLLOOn.

text: If today is Wednesday, what day will it be 100 days from now?
why: 100 days is 14 weeks and 2 days, and two days after Wednesday is Friday.

text: Name the five-letter word that can follow SUN, MOON, STAR and DAY to make four new words.
why: SUNLIGHT, MOONLIGHT, STARLIGHT and DAYLIGHT.

text: A snail climbs a 10-metre wall: 3 metres up each day, sliding 2 metres back each night. On which day does it reach the top?
why: The snail gains 1 m a day, so after 7 nights it's at 7 m and climbs the last 3 m on day 8.

text: What is the smallest number that, when written in words, has its letters in alphabetical order?
why: The letters of FORTY run F, O, R, T, Y in alphabetical order, and no number word from one to thirty-nine does.

text: What is half of two plus two?
why: You halve two first and then add two: 1 + 2 = 3.

text: A woman has two coins that add up to 30p. One of them is not a 20p. What are the coins?
why: Only one of the coins is not a 20p; the other one is, so the pair is 20p + 10p.

text: In a leap year, which month other than April starts on the same day of the week as January?
why: January to July is 31+29+31+30+31+30 = 182 days, exactly 26 weeks, so both start on the same weekday.

text: What is the next number: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ___?
why: These are the square numbers 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², so next is 6² = 36.

text: Which word is spelt wrongly in every dictionary?
why: WRONGLY is always spelt W-R-O-N-G-L-Y, so every dictionary really does spell "wrongly".

text: Six glasses in a row: the first three are full, the next three empty. Moving only ONE glass, make them alternate full and empty. Which glass do you move?
answers: Pour the second into the fifth
why: Pour glass 2 into glass 5 and put it back: the glasses then go full, empty, full, empty, full, empty.

text: What number comes next: 10, 9, 60, 90, 70, 66, ___?
why: Each is the largest number with 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 letters (TEN, NINE, SIXTY, NINETY, SEVENTY, SIXTY-SIX), so next is NINETY-SIX with 9.

text: I have keys but no locks, space but no room, and you can enter but not go inside. What am I?
why: A keyboard has keys, a space bar and an Enter key.

text: Rearrange the letters of DORMITORY to make two words that describe a messy one.
why: DORMITORY and DIRTY ROOM use the same nine letters: D, I, M, O, O, R, R, T, Y.

text: A man looks at a portrait and says 'Brothers and sisters I have none, but that man's father is my father's son.' Who is in the portrait?
why: He has no brothers, so "my father's son" is himself, which makes the man in the portrait his son.

text: What is the missing letter: A, E, F, H, I, K, L, M, N, ___? (Think about how they are written.)
answers: T - letters made of straight lines only
why: A, E, F, H, I, K, L, M and N are made only of straight lines; O, P, Q, R and S are curved, so next is T.

text: Three light switches downstairs control one bulb upstairs. You may go upstairs once. How do you tell which switch works the bulb? (One phrase.)
answers: Feel if the bulb is warm
Turn one on for a while, then off, turn another on; the warm bulb tells you
why: Leave switch 1 on for a while, turn it off, then switch 2 on: a lit bulb means 2, a warm bulb 1 and a cold bulb 3.
Pair the numbers as 1+100, 2+99 and so on: that's 50 pairs of 101, which is 5050.

text: Which common word has three consecutive double letters?
why: BOOKKEEPER has three double letters in a row: bOOKKEEper.

text: What is the next in the sequence: 1, 11, 21, 1211, 111221, ___?
why: Each term describes the one before: 111221 is "three 1s, two 2s, one 1", which gives 312211.

text: A rope ladder hangs over the side of a ship with its bottom rung touching the water. The rungs are 30 cm apart and the tide rises 90 cm an hour. After two hours, how many rungs are under water?
answers: The ship rises with the tide
why: The ship floats, so it rises with the tide, and the ladder rises too; no more rungs go under water.

text: How many 4-digit numbers can be made using the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4 once each?
why: There are 4 choices for the first digit, then 3, 2 and 1: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24.

text: What is the next number: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, ___?
why: These are the prime numbers in order, and the next prime after 13 is 17.

text: What is the smallest positive number that is divisible by every number from 1 to 10?
why: You need 2³ for the 8, 3² for the 9, plus 5 and 7: 8 × 9 × 5 × 7 = 2520.

text: Which English word contains each of the five vowels exactly once, in alphabetical order, and means 'flippant'?
why: F-A-C-E-T-I-O-U-S has A, E, I, O and U once each, in that order.

text: Two trains 100 miles apart travel toward each other at 40 and 60 mph. A fly zips between them at 80 mph until they meet. How far does the fly travel?
why: The trains close at 100 mph, so they meet after 1 hour, and in that hour the fly covers 80 miles.
These are the letter counts of ONE (3) to NINE (4), so next is TEN with 3 letters.

text: A bag has 5 red and 5 blue socks. In the dark, how many must you take to be sure of a matching pair?
why: There are only two colours, so any 3 socks must include two of the same colour.

text: In a knockout tennis tournament with 128 players, how many matches are played in total?
why: Each match knocks out one player, and 127 players must go out to leave one winner.

text: What is the only English word in everyday use that ends in the letters -MT?
why: DREAMT (the past tense of dream) is the only common word that ends in -MT.

text: You are in a race and overtake the person in second place. What place are you in now?
why: You pass the person in second place and take their spot, so you're second, not first.

text: The day before yesterday I was 25. Next year I will be 28. On what day of the year is my birthday?
why: It's 1 January. You were 25 on 30 December, turned 26 on 31 December, will be 27 this December and 28 next year.

text: What is 40 divided by half, plus 15?
why: Dividing by a half doubles: 40 ÷ ½ = 80, then 80 + 15 = 95.

text: How many people must be in a room for it to be more likely than not that two share a birthday?
why: With 23 people there are 253 possible pairs, which pushes the chance of a shared birthday just past 50% (50.7%).

text: A cube of side 3 is painted red and cut into 27 unit cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two red faces?
why: Only the middle cube on each edge has exactly two painted faces, and a cube has 12 edges.

text: Using each of the digits 1 to 9 once, the sum of a 3x3 magic square's rows is always what?
why: The digits 1 to 9 add up to 45, split equally across 3 rows: 45 ÷ 3 = 15.

text: On a 12-hour clock, how many times a day do the hour and minute hands point in exactly the same direction?
why: The hands overlap 11 times every 12 hours (never between 11 and 1), so 22 times a day.

text: What is the smallest number that can be written as the sum of two cubes in two different ways?
why: 1729 = 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³, and no smaller number can be written as two cubes in two different ways.

text: If yesterday had been Wednesday's tomorrow, and tomorrow is Sunday's yesterday, what day is today?
why: Wednesday's tomorrow is Thursday, so yesterday was Thursday; Sunday's yesterday is Saturday, so tomorrow is Saturday: today is Friday.

text: Which 7-letter word contains thousands of letters?
why: MAILBOX (M-A-I-L-B-O-X, 7 letters) holds thousands of posted letters.

text: Which is the odd one out: TRIANGLE, SQUARE, CIRCLE, PENTAGON? (Think sides.)
why: The triangle, square and pentagon have straight sides; the circle has none.

text: How many legs do three dogs, two chickens and a spider have altogether?
why: Three dogs have 12 legs, two chickens 4 and a spider 8: 12 + 4 + 8 = 24.

text: If 6 workers build a wall in 12 hours, how long would 4 workers take at the same pace?
why: 6 workers × 12 hours is 72 worker-hours, and 72 ÷ 4 = 18 hours.

text: I am a three-digit number. My tens digit is five more than my ones digit, and my hundreds digit is eight less than my tens digit. What am I?
why: The hundreds digit must be at least 1, so the tens digit is 9 and the ones digit 9 − 5 = 4, giving 194.

text: What is the next number in the sequence: 100, 50, 25, 12.5, ___?
why: Each number is half the one before: 12.5 ÷ 2 = 6.25.

text: Which of these words does NOT rhyme with the others when spoken: BOUGH, COUGH, PLOUGH, NOW?
why: BOUGH, PLOUGH and NOW all end in an "ow" sound, but COUGH is said "coff".

text: What is the missing number in this grid: 2 4 6 / 3 6 9 / 4 8 ___?
why: Each row is a times table; the third row is 4, 8, 12.

text: Which two numbers, when multiplied, give 24 and when added give 11?
A cube has how many edges?
why: A cube has 4 edges on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 upright ones: 12 in all.

text: What is 9 squared minus 8 squared, plus 7 squared minus 6 squared?
How many different ways can you arrange the letters of the word LEVEL?
why: LEVEL has 5 letters with L and E each appearing twice: 5! ÷ (2! × 2!) = 120 ÷ 4 = 30.
